notes: Review-panel diffs get their own child lane and share one git per checkout, and the renderer keeps only the mounted panes' transcripts loaded: the two main-thread loads measured on 2026-10-11 (checkpoint.status waiting 22 minutes behind the four shared slots, and a 2,560-request session.events burst on reconnect at 2.9 GB RSS) each lose their mechanism. spawnBudget.ts gains withBudget/currentBudget (an AsyncLocalStorage scope every budgeted exec reads) and a statusBudget of two slots; CheckpointStore.status (checkpoint.ts) runs under it, so twenty open panels in a 49k-file checkout can only slow each other while ensure and capture keep the shared budget, coalesces callers per session (a status already on its way answers everyone who asks meanwhile, reconnects and git-changed nudges included) and shares one `git diff --numstat` per checkout among concurrent statuses (sharedDiffIndex; ensure, capture and sync still read the index fresh because they run right after a write). The send-path audit found no await on the per-session chain or the budget in send, steer, resume, continue, turn-pass or report-drain (the only checkpoint touch is the void armBaseline), and sessions-send-baseline now proves it: a send returns in under 100 ms while a 30 s ensure and a 30 s status are both in flight for that session. The renderer store (tcserver/store.ts) learns the mounted set from App.tsx (the warm tabs' leaves): a reconnect replays only those transcripts and their subagents and unloads the rest, a transcript whose tab left the warm set unloads three seconds later (blocks and seq reset, session.unsubscribe sent; a busy session or one with a send pending keeps its rows), and PaneTree's SessionLeaf, useAgents and useSessionById re-request a transcript whose `loaded` the store dropped so a parked pane that comes back refetches on its own. ensureLoaded takes a `why` (pane, prefetch, boot, agents, byId, load, complete, resync) and more than twenty loads in ten seconds write one `transcript-burst N loads in 10s (pane=…,resync=…) loaded=… mounted=…` line to stalls.log through stall.report, so the next storm names its caller. fetchHead walks a long head in slices: session.events takes `limit` (contract.ts, Store.events appends LIMIT) and the renderer asks for 4,000 rows per call from the last seq it got, folding each slice in 2,000-row pieces with a yield between, so neither process holds a 40k-row log in one call. Tests: spawnBudget (withBudget routes nested execs to the given lane; the status lane is its own budget), checkpoint-status (status git runs on the status lane while ensure and capture stay shared; five callers over three sessions on one checkout spend one numstat, and the next burst diffs again), sessions-send-baseline storm, db-events limit, store.test (a reconnect replays only mounted transcripts and their children and unloads the rest; the grace-period unload spares a busy session and unsubscribes the dropped one; a burst reports once naming the callers; a 9,000-row head loads in three 4,000-row slices). Measured in the isolated dev instance on the migrated prod copy against a 49,185-file checkout of HSSports (its pre-cleanup commit) with 20 checkpoint.status, 6 checkpoint.sync and 6 checkpoint.ensure in flight on the same checkout: session.send returned in 57 ms with its user row at seq 1, the twenty statuses all finished together at 946–951 ms (one diff shared), ensures in 1.6 s and syncs in 2.0 s. The same boot now shows fold-backfill 368 ms, cold-move and archive-sweep 1 ms and 20 ms with nothing left to do, and first-session-list at 3.6 s with 507 sessions.
